nodes.summary: A group $G$ is rational when every element $g \in G$ is conjugate in $G$ to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$ (an element of infinite order counts as having order $0$, so for it only $k = 1$ qualifies).
nodes.title: Rational group (conjugacy form, Kourovka 15.25)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is rational if every element $g \in G$ is conjugate to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$, where an element of infinite order has order $0$, so that only $k = 1$ is coprime to it. For finite groups this is the classical equivalent form of the condition that all ordinary characters of $G$ are rational-valued.
nodes.title: Rational groups, conjugacy form

nodes.summary: There is a finite rational group with a Sylow $2$-subgroup that is not rational as a group in its own right. Here a group is rational if every element $g$ is conjugate to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$.
nodes.title: Sylow 2-subgroups of rational groups need not be rational (Kourovka 16.36)

nodes.summary: The conjecture that for every finite rational group $G$, every Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, viewed as a group in its own right, is rational. Here a group is rational if every element $g$ is conjugate to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$.
nodes.title: Darafsheh's question on Sylow 2-subgroups of rational groups (Kourovka 16.36)

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, every Sylow $2$-subgroup $P$ of the symmetric group $S_{2^n}$ on $2^n$ points is rational as a group in its own right: every $g \in P$ is conjugate within $P$ to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$.
nodes.title: Sylow 2-subgroups of the symmetric groups of degree $2^n$ are rational (Kourovka 15.25)

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$, every Sylow $2$-subgroup $P$ of the symmetric group $S_{2^n}$ on $2^n$ points is rational as a group in its own right: every $g \in P$ is conjugate within $P$ to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 15.25 (statement)
